November 2010 # **15****th** **November – 26****th** **November** # **Codelco sets its 2011 premium for China at $115/t** Codelco set its premium for China at $115/t in 2011, up by 35% y-o-y. Its premium for South Korea will rise by 32% to $98/t from $74/t this year and in Japan will also be $98/t, up from $75/t. In Europe the premium will advance by 23% to $98/t. According to earlier market expectations, the premium for China would range between $110/t and $115/t. Obviously, the final outcome reached the top-end, which indicates that Codelco is optimistic about Chinese copper demand in 2011. Moreover, CRU heard that Codelco increased its 2011cathode sales to Europe by around 200kt. That is one of the reasons why Spot premiums rose slightly

Codelco managed to successfully raise its premium for China. We were told by market insiders that some consumers were not very enthusiastic to settle annual contracts after the import premium benchmark was released. They anticipate that high and volatile copper prices may impact buying interest, which may result in negative arbitrage between SHFE and LME for a long time. However, they are also concerned about raw materials availability. We believe that Chinese contract imports will not decline next year, considering that stable cathode supply is essential to large and medium sized semis manufacturers. Traders reported that spot premium quotations for imported © 2010 CRU International Limited **confidential** **November 2010** www.crumonitor.com cathode were very volatile in the last two weeks. The latest quotations for imported cathode were around $70-100/t, with major deals closed at $70-80/t. The premium for imported EW cathode is around $6070/t. Due to the rise in the SHFE/LME cash month price ratio, the EW cathode premium quotation increased compared to a fortnight ago. In addition, traders were reluctant to reduce spot premium quotations as the annual premium has been settled at high levels. # **Chinese October refined copper consumption at lowest level since January 2010** Chinese refined copper consumption

Chinese apparent refined copper consumption fell by 13.8% m-o-m to 543,768 in October, a year-to-date low. According to CNIA data, domestic refined copper production in October amounted to 372,000t, a contraction of 4.0% m-o-m. We believe that domestic cathode output was affected by the closure of Zhongtiaoshan Nonferrous Metals Group in October due to electricity rationing. Currently, Zhongtiaoshan has 100kt/y

smelting and refining capacity. However, the production decline was limited as smelters’ raw materials (concentrate and scrap) were abundant. Moreover, Chinese refined copper imports declined significantly in October thus drugging down apparent consumption. This is attributed to the fact that the arbitrage window closed and, also, there were less working days in October. China imported 169,897t of cathode in October, a 29.7% m-o-m decline, according to the Chinese customs. We anticipate that refined copper consumption may recover in November, as high copper prices encourage smelters to raise production. The rally in spot TC/RCs is also good news for smelters. Moreover, considering seasonal patterns, refined Chinese imports tend to exhibit a m-o-m increase in November. # **Cathode stock changes in China** SHFE stocks have been on the rise since the beginning of October. According to the SHFE report, cathode inventories were 126,736t last week, up by 39,289t compared to the end of September. Then, SHFE inventories declined slightly to 122,612t, but still remained at high levels. We attribute the recent increase in exchange stocks to the following reasons. Firstly, high copper prices encouraged scrap traders to release material to the market and that impacted cathode demand. Secondly, the Shanghai physical market discount SHFE inventories decline slightly

Finally, high copper prices affected cathode demand. © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 4 **November 2010** www.crumonitor.com Cathode inventories in Shanghai bonded warehouses have been rising since the beginning of September. The SHFE/LME arbitrage has been mostly negative since the end of July and continuously negative since the end of August. We estimate that cathode inventories in Shanghai bonded warehouses are currently nearly 300,000t, up by around 100,000t since the end of September. Changes of cathode stocks held at producers, consumers and merchants exhibited different patterns. We understand that with surging copper prices, producers’ cathode inventories contracted. Cathode stocks held by consumers also saw a downward trend in October. Most semi fabricators chose to consume raw material stocks when copper prices surged. We heard reports that working stocks of semis makers were equivalent to about five to seven days of demand in October. Although fabricators replenished cathode stocks when copper prices retreated, we are told that their purchasing power remains constrained due to tight credit availability, so their cathode stocks will not increase significantly. Stock changes among different traders were not uniform s

ince they hold different expectations on future copper price levels. What we know is that speculative traders have been very active lately. In fact, they have become the main buyers in the market. To conclude, we believe that there is uncertainty regarding the time that a strong recovery in Chinese imports will take place, respecting the fact that cathode stocks are now rising. # **Copper prices may stay range bound** LME 3-month official copper prices dropped to $8,110/t in the last two weeks, mainly affected by the Chinese government’s policy to tighten liquidity in order to control inflation, sovereign debt worries in Ireland and a strong US dollar. economic data. SHFE 3-month copper prices declined to RMB61,490/t on 23rd November. On 26th November, SHFE 3-month copper prices were RMB61,670/t. Lately, commodity prices have been facing pressure from the imposition of severe Chinese regulation. The Chinese central bank announced on 24th November that domestic financial institutions need to control their credit size and limit it to normal levels. The Chinese government set a target that new loans in 2010 would be RMB7.5 trillion. However, new loans from January to October had already reached RMB6.88 trillion. For the time being, industry participants are waiting for the Political Bureau of the Central Committee of the CPC Economic Work Conference to set a tone for macroeconomic policy in 2011 at its next meeting in early December. Macroeconomic policy will primarily focus on preventing inflation and ensuring economic growth. Apart from the current financial uncertainty, SHFE supervising measures may put pressure on short term domestic copper prices as some speculative investors may close their positions. SHFE announced that it will raise the futures contracts trading margin and trading limits, effective from 29th November 2010. © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 4 **November 2010** www.crumonitor.com After the adjustment, the copper futures contracts trading margin will be 10% and that of trading limits 6%. We believe that copper prices are supported by the fundamentals, even though there are frequent releases of negative financial news. We expect the SHFE 3-month copper price to range between RMB62,000-65,000/y in the next two weeks. ## **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** ## **Grace Qu (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2206, ext. 321 ## grace.qu@crugroup.com **Panos Kotseras (London):** +44 20 7903 2077 panayiotis.kotseras@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 26th November, 2010.
